subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the lengths of the subtangent and the subnormal to the curve y = b sin(x/a) at any point.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what dy/dx is, which of the two lengths divides and which multiplies, and the double-angle identity you use at the end.

steps.label: Differentiate and state the definitions
steps.margin_note: First mark. The chain rule gives the factor 1/a from the angle x/a. Write both definitions here so that neither part starts from a guess.
lines: Differentiate with respect to x. The angle x/a differentiates to 1/a:
At a point (x, y) with m = dy/dx:
subtangent = y/m   and   subnormal = y · m

recall.must_convey: That dy/dx = (b/a)cos(x/a), and that subtangent = y/m, subnormal = ym.
accept: differentiate sin of x by a to cos of x by a times one by a
dy by dx is b by a into cos x by a
the subtangent is y by m and the subnormal is y into m
chain rule tho one by a bayataki vasthundi
sine differentiates to cosine and the angle gives one by a

steps.why: The angle is x/a, not x, so the chain rule contributes 1/a. Both lengths are built from the same y and the same m, so they are set up together.
common_mistakes: Writing dy/dx = b cos(x/a) and omitting the 1/a.
Writing dy/dx = ab cos(x/a), multiplying by a instead of dividing.
Differentiating sin(x/a) to −cos(x/a), using the cosine rule by mistake.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiate the sine first, then multiply by the derivative of the angle. Here the angle x/a gives 1/a.

steps.label: Length of the subtangent
steps.margin_note: Second mark. b cancels between numerator and denominator, and sin ÷ cos leaves a tangent. The a in the denominator of m moves up and multiplies.
lines: ∴ length of the subtangent = a tan(x/a)

recall.must_convey: That y/m simplifies to a tan(x/a).
accept: divide y by m and b cancels
the subtangent is a tan of x by a
b cancel avuthundi, a tan x by a vasthundi
the a from the denominator comes up
length of the subtangent is a times tan x by a

steps.why: Dividing by b/a multiplies by a/b, so the b's cancel and one a is left in front. What remains is sin over cos, which is the tangent of the same angle.
common_mistakes: Writing the subtangent as (1/a)tan(x/a), keeping a in the denominator.
Leaving the answer as b sin(x/a) ÷ (b/a)cos(x/a) without simplifying.
Writing tan(x)/a, changing the angle from x/a to x.
steps.memory_tip: Dividing by b/a is multiplying by a/b. The b's cancel and the a lands in front of the tangent.

steps.label: Length of the subnormal
steps.margin_note: The last two marks: one for the product (b²/a)sin(x/a)cos(x/a), one for writing it as a single sine with the double-angle identity. Both forms are correct, but the simplified one is what the question asks for.
lines: Length of the subnormal = y · m
Use  2 sin A cos A = sin 2A  with  A = x/a,  so sin(x/a)cos(x/a) = (1/2)sin(2x/a):

recall.must_convey: That ym = (b²/a)sin(x/a)cos(x/a), which the double-angle identity turns into (b²/2a)sin(2x/a).
accept: multiply y by m to get b squared by a sin cos
two sin a cos a is sin two a
the subnormal is b squared by two a into sin of two x by a
double angle formula use chesi sin two x by a ga rasta
sin cos becomes half of sin double the angle
the final answer has b squared over two a

steps.why: Multiplying y by m keeps both the sine and the cosine, and the standard identity 2 sin A cos A = sin 2A folds them into a single term. The angle doubles from x/a to 2x/a, and the extra 2 goes into the denominator.
common_mistakes: Writing sin(x/a)cos(x/a) = sin(2x/a) without the factor of one half.
Doubling the whole expression instead of the angle, giving sin(2x)/a.
Leaving the coefficient as b²/a instead of b²/2a after using the identity.
steps.memory_tip: sin A cos A is half of sin 2A. Whenever a sine and a cosine of the SAME angle multiply, that identity shortens the answer.
